subject.title: [Feature]: Memory indexing lacks checkpoint/resume capability for long-running operations

question: Should memory-core implement checkpoint/resume as a validated resumable shadow generation, as direct incremental writes to the live DB, or defer resumable full reindexing for now?
rationale: Source inspection proves the gap, but the fix changes durable memory index generation identity, incomplete-index status/search semantics, and possibly public memorySearch config, so automation should not choose the product contract.

options.title: Resumable shadow generation
options.body: Persist generation/checkpoint state for the shadow DB and publish only after validation, preserving the current safe-rebuild invariant while allowing restart resume.

options.title: Direct incremental live writes
options.body: Write checkpointed progress into the live DB with explicit incomplete-generation filtering and status semantics, accepting a larger migration and config surface.

options.title: Defer resume support
options.body: Keep the current atomic full rebuild behavior and rely on embedding-cache reuse and stale-shadow cleanup until maintainers prioritize a broader memory indexing redesign.

recommendation.title: Resumable shadow generation
recommendation.body: Persist generation/checkpoint state for the shadow DB and publish only after validation, preserving the current safe-rebuild invariant while allowing restart resume.

likelyOwner.reason: The earlier safe reindex lineage and prior keep-open review both route the product-shape decision most directly to steipete.
